steps.do:
Decide eligible_for_provisional_credit for each dispute using the Provisional Credit Eligibility Guidelines. Every criterion must hold:
(1) The account has been open at least 60 days: open date from get_accounts to today from get_time.
(2) The reason is unauthorized_fraudulent_charge or duplicate_charge, or it is goods_services_not_received with a purchase date from the records more than 30 days before today.
(3) The amount is at least $25.00 and no more than the tier maximum of the card the transaction is on: Entry $2500.00, Mid $5000.00, Premium $10000.00, Elite $15000.00, Invitation $25000.00.
(4) No more than 2 disputes in the past 12 months (check_dispute_history, or running_dispute_count when several disputes are filed).
(5) For a reason other than fraud, the merchant was contacted.
If any criterion fails, set it to false.

verify.why: The policy requires 2 of the 4 values to match and says to share nothing before verification.

clauses.clause: Share nothing before they match; if they do not match, do not continue
clauses.source: Policy: 'Do not leak any information about the user before they are verified.' Doc 026 Freezing Requirement 1: 'Customer must be verified'.

get_time.why: Policy guideline 4 and the get_current_time description require this tool for the verification timestamp.

clauses.clause: get current time for the verification log
clauses.source: Policy 4 says to 'always use the get_current_time() tool'. The tool description says 'Use this to get the current timestamp for logging verification records.'

log_verif.why: The policy and the log_verification description require logging after verification.

clauses.clause: log after 2 values match
clauses.source: Policy: 'After verification, you must call the verification logging tool'. The tool description says to call it 'after you have verified a user by confirming 2 out of 4 identity fields'.

get_accounts.why: Doc 009 names this tool for retrieving checking accounts, and the step asks the customer when the account is unclear instead of guessing.

get_cards.why: Doc 028 names this tool and lists its fields, and says to check the card's status before freezing or unfreezing.

advise_close.why: Doc 026 says to recommend closing for a card confirmed lost or stolen, and its Freezing vs. Closing passage sets which choice applies when.

clauses.clause: not still searching
clauses.source: Doc 026: 'FREEZE... Use when customer misplaced the card'. Its Reasons for Freezing include 'Customer misplaced the card and is looking for it'. So a customer still searching is in the freeze case, not the confirmed-lost case.

clauses.clause: then do what the customer chooses
clauses.source: Doc 026 says 'recommend closing instead of freezing'. A recommendation leaves the choice with the customer, and the doc covers both paths: 'Procedure for when a customer wants to temporarily freeze' and 'CLOSE... Use when card is confirmed lost/stolen'.

credit_cards_named_with_debit.why: Doc 026 covers debit cards only, and doc 030 gives the credit-card protection for lost or stolen cards after the debit freeze or close.

clauses.clause: lost or stolen, including a wallet the customer is still searching for
clauses.source: Doc 030 applies 'When a customer reports a lost or stolen debit card'. Its step 1 is 'Complete the standard debit card freeze/close procedure', which includes the freeze. Doc 026 uses the freeze 'when customer misplaced the card'. So a lost card that is still being searched for is in doc 030's scope.

clauses.clause: For any other freeze reason, say no procedure was found
clauses.source: No document gives a credit-card freeze procedure. Policy 1 says: 'If you cannot find relevant information, let the user know.'

misplaced_freeze_first.why: Doc 026 names the freeze for a customer who misplaced the card and is looking for it, and names closing once the card is confirmed lost or stolen.

check_freeze.why: Doc 026 Freezing Requirements 2 and 3 state the owner check and the ACTIVE-only check.

clauses.clause: skip it and tell the customer why
clauses.source: Doc 026 Freezing Requirement 3: 'cannot freeze PENDING, CLOSED, or already FROZEN cards'. The freeze_debit_card_3892 description lists these same cases as errors.

freeze_info.why: Every item is stated in doc 026 Freezing Step 3.

freeze.why: Doc 026 Freezing Step 4 states the call, and doc 031 adds the dispute-driven freeze.

clauses.clause: or its most severe filed-dispute card_action is freeze_pending_investigation

confirm_freeze.why: Doc 026 Freezing Step 5 states the confirmation, and its Important Notes state the ATM points.

cross_product_after_freeze.why: Doc 030 requires the credit-card check after the debit freeze or close for a lost or stolen card.

clauses.clause: including a wallet the customer is still searching for
clauses.source: Doc 030's trigger is 'reports a lost or stolen debit card', and its step 1 is the 'freeze/close procedure'. Doc 026 uses the freeze 'when customer misplaced the card'. So a lost card still being searched for is covered.

debit_changes_before_cross_product.why: Doc 030 puts the debit procedure first, and doc 026 allows an unfreeze or a close only when the customer wants it.

clauses.clause: Do not unfreeze a card the customer has not asked to unfreeze
clauses.source: Doc 026's procedure is 'for when a customer wants to... unfreeze'. No passage allows an unfreeze the customer did not ask for.

clauses.clause: Do not close a card the customer has not confirmed lost or stolen or asked to cancel

clauses.clause: tell the customer it could not be completed and why
clauses.source: The freeze_debit_card_3892 and unfreeze_debit_card_3893 descriptions list the error replies, including 'already frozen', the current status and 'no longer open'.

reread_cards_unfreeze.why: Doc 028 Use Case 3 says to verify the card exists and check its current status before unfreezing.

check_unfreeze.why: Doc 026 Unfreezing Requirements 2, 3 and 4 state each check.

clauses.clause: stop if a check fails
clauses.source: Doc 026 lists these as Unfreezing Requirements. The unfreeze_debit_card_3893 description gives errors for a card that is not FROZEN and for an account that is no longer open.

unfreeze.why: Doc 026 Unfreezing Step 2 states the call, and the step's conditions match the Unfreezing Requirements.

clauses.clause: customer has found the card and asks to unfreeze it
clauses.source: Doc 026's procedure covers 'when a customer wants to... unfreeze'. No passage names this job's case, a card frozen as lost and not yet recovered, so the hold on unfreezing an unrecovered card stays.

unfreeze_from_review.why: Doc 003 sends the customer's yes into this protocol, and doc 026 Unfreezing Step 2 and its requirements govern the call.

return_to_decline_review.why: Once unfrozen the card is ACTIVE, and doc 003's ACTIVE branch continues to the remaining checks in order.

clauses.clause: continue with the account status, fraud alert and velocity checks
clauses.source: Doc 026 Unfreezing Step 3: 'Confirm the card is now active'. Doc 003: 'Check the following IN ORDER' and 'If status is ACTIVE → Continue to step 2.' Steps 2 to 4 of doc 003 are the account status, fraud alert and velocity checks.

handoff_close.why: The step closes only a card that is both confirmed lost or stolen and asked to be cancelled, but doc 026 names each case separately as a reason to close.

clauses.clause: confirms are lost or stolen and asks to cancel
clauses.source: Doc 026: 'CLOSE... Use when card is confirmed lost/stolen or customer wants to cancel.' This passage names a customer who wants to cancel as its own case. Requiring both conditions contradicts it, and it also contradicts this job's debit_changes_before_cross_product step.

clauses.clause: Never close a card the customer has found and wants to keep
clauses.source: Doc 026 limits closing to cards confirmed lost or stolen, or cards the customer wants to cancel. A found card the customer wants to keep is neither.

rewrite.do: For each frozen card the customer either confirms is lost or stolen and agrees to close after the closing recommendation, or asks to cancel, go on to closing_cancelling_a_debit_card. Never close a card the customer has found and wants to keep.

clauses.source: Policy 6: 'If the user asks for a human agent 4 times' counts every request in the conversation. So a request in the opening message counts, and the count runs from the first message.

clauses.clause: Do not transfer on the 1st to 3rd request
clauses.source: Policy 6 says 'kindly inform the user that you can help them, and try to help them first'. The transfer permission starts only at 4 requests. No passage allows a transfer earlier while the issue is within the agent's capabilities.

transfer_on_fourth_request.why: Policy 6 permits the transfer at the 4th request, the tool description defines the summary, and doc 042 defines how to choose the reason code.

clauses.clause: summary content

clauses.clause: the most accurate code from the highest applicable tier
clauses.source: Doc 042 says: 'select the most accurate reason code ... always select from the highest tier that applies.'

clauses.clause: reuse earlier verification

from_dispute_card_action.why: Doc 031 says the most severe card action is performed once per card after filing, and a freeze is that action when freeze_pending_investigation is the most severe.

clauses.source: Doc 031 says: 'when performing the actual card action after filing all disputes, use the MOST SEVERE action', followed by '... call freeze_debit_card_3892 (the most severe action) once for the card.'

clauses.clause: do not verify again
clauses.source: The policy says 'No need to verify more than once in a single conversation.'

clauses.clause: ask for name and two identity values; look up by name, email or id

The get_user_information_by_name tool description says it is 'Case Sensitive'. 3. The by_email and by_id tools return the same fields.

verify.why: The policy requires 2 of the 4 identity values to match and forbids leaking information before verification.

clauses.clause: if they do not match, do not continue
clauses.source: 1. Doc 026 lists 'Customer must be verified' as a freezing requirement and an unfreezing requirement. 2. The policy says 'Do not leak any information about the user before they are verified.'

advise_close.why: Doc 026 says to recommend closing when the loss is confirmed, and a recommendation leaves the choice with the customer.

clauses.clause: not still searching

clauses.clause: for any other freeze reason, say no procedure was found
clauses.source: Policy 1 says: 'If you cannot find relevant information, let the user know.'

clauses.clause: once the customer agrees
clauses.source: Doc 026 describes the procedure as being for when 'a customer wants to temporarily freeze', so the freeze waits for the customer's consent.

clauses.clause: tell the customer the card cannot be frozen and why, and skip it

cross_product_after_freeze.why: Doc 030 orders the credit card check after the debit freeze/close procedure for a lost or stolen report.

clauses.clause: including a wallet the customer is still searching for
clauses.source: 1. Doc 030 is triggered by 'reports a lost or stolen debit card'. 2. Its step 1 includes freeze, which Doc 026 uses for a misplaced card.

debit_changes_before_cross_product.why: Doc 030 puts the debit freeze/close procedure first, and Doc 026 limits unfreezing to a customer's request and closing to a confirmed loss or a cancel request.

clauses.clause: Do not unfreeze a card the customer has not asked to unfreeze
clauses.source: Doc 026 describes the procedure as for when 'a customer wants to ... unfreeze'. No passage unfreezes a card without the customer's request.

clauses.clause: Do not close a card not confirmed lost/stolen or asked to cancel
clauses.source: Doc 026 says CLOSE is used 'when card is confirmed lost/stolen or customer wants to cancel'.

clauses.clause: transfer only if they say yes
clauses.source: Policy 5 says: 'ask the user whether they would like to be transferred ... Do not transfer without asking the user first.'

rules: A card must be ACTIVE or PENDING to be closed
Pending transactions block a closure
Lost, stolen and fraud reasons bypass the card-age rule (requirement 6)
A pending refund blocks closure unless the customer waits or acknowledges in writing
Refunds to a closed card go to the linked checking account
Lost or stolen cards close immediately
The card must belong to the verified user
Perform one action per card: the most severe among its disputes
Only an ACTIVE card can be frozen
Entry tier: 48-hour wait after closure
Tiers other than Entry have no wait
Fees are charged to checking when the card is ordered
Entry tier accounts
Bluest is Elite tier
For a lost or stolen card, recommend closing rather than freezing
Closed cards cannot be reopened
A CRITICAL card cannot be unlocked; recommend closure
With no unauthorized transactions, close only if the customer chooses to

verdicts.clause: all
verdicts.why: derived: the lookup quote and the 'Before closing a card: Confirm the card_id and current status' quote support the read, and the passage around them names issue_reason as a field to look up.

verdicts.clause: Do not clear a customer-initiated fraud alert on a card with a filed fraud dispute
verdicts.why: derived: doc 003 clears a customer-initiated alert only if the customer confirms all transactions are legitimate, and a filed fraud dispute means they have not.

verdicts.clause: Close the card with reason fraud_suspected
verdicts.why: derived: doc 031 maps fraud dispute categories to close_and_reissue and requires the agent to perform that action, and doc 025 lists suspected fraud as a closing reason.

verdicts.clause: If it was reported lost or stolen ... If a replacement card with status PENDING exists, guide them through activating it
verdicts.why: Doc 037 gives the pending-replacement activation only in the lost-card branch; its stolen branch requires enhanced verification and then offers to order a replacement, so the lost rule is carried to stolen.

verdicts.clause: a found card whose filed disputes give close_and_reissue
verdicts.why: derived: doc 031 requires the agent to perform the indicated card action after filing the dispute, and doc 026 says CLOSE is used when the customer wants to cancel or the card is confirmed lost or stolen.

verdicts.clause: Lost, stolen and fraud_suspected bypass this card-age check (requirement 6); checks 1 to 4 still apply to them
verdicts.unsupported: checks 3 (pending transactions) ... still apply to them
verdicts.why: Doc 025 waives only requirement 6, but for these reasons it says to inform the customer that pending transactions will still be processed and that lost or stolen cards are closed immediately, so pending transactions do not block closure for them.

verdicts.clause: There are no pending transactions other than refunds
verdicts.why: Requirement 4 bars any pending or processing transactions and sets no exception for refunds; refunds are handled separately in requirement 5.

verdicts.clause: A FROZEN card is unfrozen first
verdicts.why: derived: closure requires ACTIVE or PENDING status (doc 025), and unfreezing a FROZEN card makes it active (doc 026).

verdicts.clause: closure is blocked by check_elig ... freeze the card
verdicts.unsupported: closure is blocked by check_elig (as the trigger to offer a freeze); card status is ACTIVE, belongs to the verified user
verdicts.why: Doc 026 supports freezing for a misplaced card or for temporary security, but no quote ties a freeze offer to blocked closure or states the freeze requirements.

verdicts.clause: all
verdicts.why: Each clause is quoted directly from doc 025 step 4 for lost, stolen and fraud_suspected.

verdicts.clause: close it in close_card with reason fraud_suspected; only once
verdicts.why: derived: doc 041 says to close the card when unauthorized transactions are found, doc 025 lists suspected fraud/unauthorized transactions as the closing reason, and a closed card cannot be closed again.

verdicts.clause: unfreeze then close
verdicts.why: derived: closure requires ACTIVE or PENDING status (025 req 3), and doc 026 gives the unfreeze tool and its requirement that the account be OPEN.

verdicts.clause: Use reason fraud_suspected when unauthorized transactions were found

verdicts.clause: pick_action gave close_and_reissue
verdicts.why: derived: doc 031 requires the agent to perform the indicated card action, and doc 025 gives close_debit_card_4721 for closing.

verdicts.why: The only quote says lost or stolen cards are closed immediately with no cooling-off period; it states neither the pending-transaction check (which doc 025 says does not block these reasons) nor an unfreeze step.

check_unauth.why: Doc 041 Step 6.1 orders the check, and the customer's answer decides which transactions are unauthorized.

clauses.clause: successful = posted or pending, not the declined types

clauses.source: Doc 041 Step 6.1 says 'suspicious period' and Step 2 ties the lock to the declined attempts. The window starts there. Because the period has no stated end, the customer is also asked about other recent transactions, so nothing is excluded.

dispute.why: Doc 041 Step 6.2 orders the filing; doc 031, doc 032 and the tool description fix each argument.

clauses.clause: card_present_fraud for an ATM or in-store transaction

clauses.clause: disputed_amount = absolute recorded amount
clauses.source: Doc 018: debits are negative. Tool: 'disputed_amount must be a positive number.' So the absolute value is used.

clauses.clause: liability: lesser of $50 / $500 and the amount, or -1
clauses.source: Doc 031: $50 within 2 business days of statement, $500 within 60 days, unlimited after. Tool: maximum liability is 'based on Regulation E reporting timing rules and the disputed amount. Use -1 for unlimited'. A customer cannot be liable for more than the amount.

clauses.clause: otherwise present the options without recommending one
clauses.source: Doc 041 marks closure 'recommended if fraud suspected' and recommends it at CRITICAL. No passage recommends any option in other cases.

pin_lock_close_no_dispute.why: Doc 041 Step 6.3 lets the customer choose closure, doc 025 governs the reason and eligibility, and doc 041 scores each card individually.

clauses.clause: file no dispute; skip reread_disputes and pick_action
clauses.source: Doc 041 Step 6.2 files disputes only 'If unauthorized transactions found'. Here none were found, so no dispute exists to set a card action.

clauses.clause: close through check_elig and close_card
clauses.source: Doc 025 Closing Step 3: check eligibility before closing. Step 5: close with close_debit_card_4721.

pick_action.why: For a PIN-locked card whose filed disputes are all unauthorized_transaction, the step performs a freeze, but doc 041 names this case and says to close the card.

clauses.clause: perform the most severe filed card_action (freeze_pending_investigation) on a PIN-locked card whose unauthorized-transaction disputes came from the PIN lock investigation
clauses.source: Doc 041 Step 6.2 names this case: 'If unauthorized transactions found: File dispute, close card, order replacement.' Doc 031's severity rule also puts close_and_reissue above freeze_pending_investigation.

clauses.clause: decide each card on its own
clauses.source: Doc 031: the most severe action is taken across the disputes on the same card. Doc 041: 'Each card must be scored individually'.

rewrite.do: For each card with filed disputes, take the most severe card_action among them (close_and_reissue > freeze_pending_investigation > keep_active) and perform it once per card. Decide each card on its own. A PIN-locked card that cannot be unlocked and has disputes filed for successful unauthorized transactions on it is closed (pin_lock_close_once, close_card), even if its disputes map only to freeze_pending_investigation. Do not freeze it.
rewrite.if: the job follows disputes filed in this conversation

basis.quote: Severity order (highest to lowest): 'close_and_reissue' > 'freeze_pending_investigation' > 'keep_active'.
However, when performing the actual card action after filing all disputes, use the MOST SEVERE action across all disputes.
2. If unauthorized transactions found: File dispute, close card, order replacement.
Each card must be scored individually and may have different outcomes.

unfiled_dispute_ignored.why: Doc 031 sets card_action at filing and performs the action after filing, so a dispute that was not filed contributes nothing.

clauses.clause: unfiled disputes set no card action
clauses.source: Doc 031: card_action is a filing parameter, and the action is performed 'after filing all disputes' across those disputes.

clauses.clause: all keep_active: card stays active
clauses.source: Doc 031 mapping and severity order: if every filed dispute maps to keep_active, the most severe action is keep_active.

alert_card_not_cleared.why: Doc 003 clears a customer-initiated alert only when the customer confirms all transactions are legitimate, which a filed fraud dispute contradicts, and doc 031 requires closure for close_and_reissue.

clauses.clause: do not clear the alert
clauses.source: Doc 003: 'If they confirm all transactions are legitimate, clear the alert.' A filed fraud dispute means the customer has not confirmed that.

clauses.source: Doc 025 lists the reason 'Suspected fraud/unauthorized transactions', which is the value fraud_suspected. Doc 041: 'likely fraud'.

inform_pending.why: Doc 025 Closing Step 4 states all three items for these reasons.

clauses.source: Doc 041 names declined types 'atm_withdrawal_declined'/'pos_declined'. Doc 018 gives statuses 'posted' or 'pending'. So successful transactions are the non-declined ones.

clauses.source: Doc 041 D1 and Step 5: '3+ prior locks: Cannot unlock. Must reset PIN.' This names the case, so for it the step must say a PIN reset is required. For all other non-CRITICAL, non-fraud cases the clause is kept.

clauses.clause: Recommend closure when the score was CRITICAL
clauses.source: Doc 041 table, 15+ CRITICAL: 'Recommend card closure and replacement.'

rewrite.do: Explain the security concern without revealing the scoring. Offer card closure and replacement, a transfer to the security team, or a PIN reset. Recommend closure when the score was CRITICAL or fraud is suspected. If the card has 3 or more prior PIN locks in the last 90 days, tell the customer a PIN reset is required for this card; closure and replacement remain available. Otherwise present the options without recommending one.
rewrite.quote: 3. If no unauthorized transactions: Explain the security concern and offer options:

basis.quote: 3. If no unauthorized transactions: Explain the security concern and offer options:
Card closure and replacement (recommended if fraud suspected)
15+ | CRITICAL | CANNOT unlock. Check for successful unauthorized transactions. Recommend card closure and replacement.
Cannot unlock. Must reset PIN.

clauses.clause: If a check fails, explain what blocks the order and stop
clauses.source: Doc 023 lists these as eligibility requirements, and step 3 checks them before ordering at step 7. An unmet requirement therefore blocks the order, and policy guideline 1 says to tell the user.

old_card_not_closed.why: A card whose closure was blocked stays ACTIVE or PENDING, which blocks the order; for a FROZEN card no passage decides, so the prohibition is kept.

clauses.clause: do not order when closure was blocked because the card is FROZEN
clauses.source: The close_debit_card_4721 description refuses non-ACTIVE/PENDING cards, so a FROZEN card cannot be closed. Doc 023 eligibility names only active and pending cards and no passage names FROZEN cards for ordering, so the prohibition stays.

clauses.clause: a new card can be ordered once the old card is closed

clauses.source: Policy guideline 1: 'If you cannot find relevant information, let the user know.' Policy guideline 5: if the issue cannot be resolved, ask whether they want a transfer.

clauses.source: Doc 029 sets 'Maximum 2 (3, 5) replacement cards per rolling 12-month period'. With N already counted, the new replacement would be card N+1, which exceeds the limit. That triggers the 'exceeded the N-card limit' options.

excess_fee_choice_step.why: The fee-or-wait choice and the fee notice are stated in doc 029, and the age-out date follows from date_issued and the rolling 12-month window.

clauses.clause: age-out date is oldest counted card's date_issued plus 12 months
clauses.source: Doc 029 says the limit runs over a 'rolling 12-month period', counts by date_issued, and requires waiting 'until oldest replacement ages out'.

clauses.source: Policy guideline 5: ask whether the user wants a transfer if the issue cannot be resolved, and 'Do not transfer without asking the user first'.

clauses.clause: technical_system_error for a system error, otherwise highest applicable tier

changelog.why: rewritten by the post-merge audit: No passage says to file every qualifying dispute before the non-qualifying ones; that order changes which disputes get provisional credit, so it must come from the customer.; logged by code (s30 merge bench)

rules: Provisional credit is true only if ALL of these hold: (1) the account has been open at least 60 days; (2) the reason is unauthorized_fraudulent_charge or duplicate_charge, or it is goods_services_not_received with the purchase made more than 30 days ago; (3) the amount is at least $25.00 and no more than the tier maximum; (4) no more than 2 disputes in the past 12 months; (5) for a non-fraud dispute, the merchant was contacted first
The reasons incorrect_amount, goods_services_not_as_described, canceled_subscription_still_charging and refund_never_processed are never eligible for provisional credit
Mid-tier cards (Silver Rewards, Business Silver Rewards, Green Rewards, Silver Zoom) have a provisional credit maximum of $5000.00
Entry-tier cards (Bronze Rewards, EcoCard, Business Bronze Rewards, Crypto-Cash Back) have a provisional credit maximum of $2500.00
Premium-tier cards (Gold Rewards, Business Gold Rewards) have a provisional credit maximum of $10000.00
Elite-tier cards (Platinum Rewards, Business Platinum Rewards) have a provisional credit maximum of $15000.00
The Invitation-tier card (Diamond Elite) has a provisional credit maximum of $25000.00
Use cancel_and_reissue only when the customer wants the card replaced; otherwise use keep_active
A card whose replacement was already ordered in this conversation takes card_action cancel_and_reissue, and no second replacement is ordered
partial_refund_amount is passed only when resolution_requested is partial_refund
partial_refund_amount is the part of that transaction in dispute (for incorrect_amount, the charge minus the expected amount) and never more than the transaction amount
If the customer does not have the last 4 digits, give them the get_card_last_4_digits user tool instead of walking them through the steps
Provisional credit requires the credit card account to have been open at least 60 days (open date from get_credit_card_accounts_by_user, compared with get_current_time)
goods_services_not_received is eligible only when the purchase was made more than 30 days ago
The transaction amount must be >= $25.00 and <= the maximum for the tier of the card it is on
Count disputes filed in the past 12 months, including those filed earlier in this conversation. A dispute meets the criterion only if the running count is 2 or less when it is filed.
For any reason other than unauthorized_fraudulent_charge, provisional credit requires contacted_merchant = true
Ordering a replacement cancels the old card automatically, so order one only when the customer wants the card replaced
Do not order a replacement unless the eligibility check (pending orders, tier limit) passes
The dispute's address argument is the registered home address from the records, never a shipping address the customer gives for a replacement card
A charge that appears more than once is a duplicate_charge
Each dispute uses the last 4 digits and tier of the card its own transaction was made on

An active dispute or a pending replacement order on the same account fails a credit limit increase eligibility check. If the customer also wants an increase that is not yet decided, ask which request comes first without telling them about the increase's eligibility checks.
Verify identity once per conversation; a later job in the same conversation reuses the verified user
A transfer after a failed filing, made only with the customer's agreement, uses reason code technical_system_error
If the dispute history read fails or returns partial data, retry it; if it still fails, escalate rather than guess the prior-dispute count

steps.do: For each dispute, decide eligible_for_provisional_credit. It is true only if ALL of these hold. (1) The card account has been open at least 60 days (date opened against dp_time). (2) The reason is unauthorized_fraudulent_charge or duplicate_charge, or goods_services_not_received when the purchase is more than 30 days old. (3) The amount is at least $25.00 and no more than the card tier's maximum: Entry (Bronze, EcoCard, Business Bronze, Crypto-Cash Back) $2500.00; Mid $5000.00; Premium (Gold, Business Gold) $10000.00; Elite $15000.00; Diamond Elite $25000.00. (4) The customer has filed no more than 2 disputes in the 12 months before this filing (dp_history plus any filed in this conversation). (5) For any reason other than unauthorized_fraudulent_charge, the customer contacted the merchant first.
